prompt: The single highest-signal artifact in an AI project portfolio is…

options.text: …an evals/ folder with a representative dataset, graders, and honestly reported results

explanation: Evals prove you measure what you build: the discipline employers struggle to hire for and tutorials never produce.

prompt: Why do three deep projects beat twelve shallow ones in a portfolio?

options.text: Depth in evaluations, failure handling, and decision records provides verifiable evidence of engineering judgment; project count alone does not
They don't; more is always better

explanation: The scarce skill is making systems trustworthy, not making models respond. Depth carries that signal; a dozen weekend demos carry none.

prompt: Reporting '92% accuracy; fails on handwritten invoices; failure analysis below' rather than 'high accuracy' is strategically smart because…

options.text: …honest limits read as senior, survive technical probing, and lend credibility to the claims that ARE strong; inflated claims collapse in the first screen
…it lowers expectations so any job feels easy

explanation: Interviews probe claims two questions deep. Measured honesty is the presentation style of people who've actually operated systems.

prompt: In an AI system-design interview, the strongest opening move is…

options.text: …clarifying the job: who uses it, at what volume, and what an error costs: before proposing any architecture

explanation: Requirements before architecture signals seniority in thirty seconds, and the answers genuinely change the right design.

prompt: Which elements belong in a winning AI system-design answer? Select all that apply.

options.text: A small eval set before any tuning
Deterministic steps where possible; the model only where ambiguity earns it
Approval gates on consequential actions, and named failure modes (retrieval miss, provider outage, injection)
A promise that the model won't make mistakes

explanation: Evals, workflow-first judgment, and volunteered risk analysis are the three senior signals. Promising a mistake-free model signals the opposite.

prompt: Asked about a tool you've never used, the strongest interview response is…

options.text: …admit the gap, then reason from primitives: what it must solve, what you'd measure on your eval set, what risks you'd check

explanation: They're hiring your process for the unknown: daily life in this field. Honest gap + transferable framework routinely outscores cached facts; bluffs die on the second probe.

prompt: For someone currently employed in a non-AI role, the most reliable route to production AI experience is usually…

options.text: …building a measured, guarded automation for their own team's workflow: domain knowledge, data access, and a willing first user are advantages outside candidates lack

explanation: The internal transition converts existing access into production evidence (and negotiating leverage) without passing anyone's résumé filter first.

prompt: The first-90-days playbook prioritizes a boring high-volume workflow over a flashy agent project because…

options.text: …trust compounds from delivered, measured, adopted wins, and low-blast-radius, high-ROI automations are where those live; earned trust then funds ambition

explanation: The unadopted impressive demo is the classic new-AI-hire failure. A grateful team saying 'this saved us 30 hours a week' is career capital.

prompt: When reporting AI work to leadership, the effective framing is…

options.text: …outcomes: cycle time, error rate, hours saved, and the human controls in place
…the architecture: models, rerankers, and frameworks used

explanation: Leadership funds outcomes. 'Deployed a RAG agent' earns a nod; 'cut cycle time 80% with approvals on payments' earns the next project.

prompt: Freelance AI automation work is priced most effectively…

options.text: …on the value of hours and errors saved (the measured ROI), not on your hours spent
…as low as possible to win volume

explanation: Your Module 13 ROI table IS the sales deck: a workflow saving €4,000/month justifies value pricing regardless of build hours.

prompt: In a coding interview where AI assistants are permitted, interviewers are primarily watching…

options.text: …how you specify, review, and verify the generated code: the failure-path checks and edge-case tests you apply
…how large a prompt you can write

explanation: AI-permitted interviews test the review discipline from Module 1: read every line, test the edges, verify unfamiliar APIs. That's the on-the-job skill.

prompt: Which job posts signal a team where this course's skills fit best?

options.text: Ones mentioning evals, reliability, production LLM features, or human-in-the-loop: regardless of exact title

explanation: Titles are noisy; job descriptions aren't. Teams that talk about evaluation and production reliability are the ones practicing this course's discipline.

prompt: The interview stage that most directly reuses your capstone preparation is…

options.text: …the judgment/behavioral round: its questions are the oral-defense prompts (biggest error source? highest blast radius? why an LLM at all?)
…none; interviews and the course are unrelated

explanation: You rehearsed the hard questions while defending your capstone. The interview asks them with a logo attached.

prompt: The career habit this course says compounds most over years is…

options.text: …keep building small end-to-end things, evaluate new techniques on your own data, and write publicly about what you learn

explanation: Primitives + evals + building + a public record of judgment: the same durable layer from Module 17, applied to a career.
